没想到 Jason Wei 已经离开 Meta，去 AI 数据公司 Mercor 当首席科学家

美国时间 11 月 17 日，Mercor CEO Brendan Foody 宣布，Jason Wei 出任首席科学家，负责组建研究团队，主管数据和评测。Jason Wei 随后发帖确认：在 Meta TBD 实验室待了一年，“训练 AI 模型的公司比以往任何时候都多，数据会决定下一个前沿”。

Jason Wei 在 Google Brain 时是思维链论文的第一作者，让模型先写推理步骤再给答案，这个做法后来被广泛使用。之后他在 OpenAI 参与了 o1 和深度研究，2025 年 7 月被 Meta 重金挖走。

他另一个强项是给 AI“出题”。他主导的 SimpleQA 测模型会不会瞎编，BrowseComp 测 AI 能不能翻遍网页找到冷门答案，都成了各家发模型时常用的评测，他还参与了医生打分的 HealthBench。他在博客里写过一条“验证者法则”：一项任务越容易验证，就越容易训练 AI 学会。

Mercor 做的正是这门生意：平台上有 500 多万名医生、律师、工程师，帮 AI 公司出题、写标准答案、给模型打分。11 月 10 日它刚融了 7.5 亿美元，估值 200 亿美元，一年翻倍。现在不只大实验室，越来越多企业拿开源模型自己训练，都需要这类数据和评测。Mercor 10 月起组建研究团队，LoRA 作者 Edward Hu 已经加入。

对 Meta 来说有点尴尬。TBD 实验室由 Scale AI 创始人 Alexandr Wang 领导，Meta 2025 年花 143 亿美元买下 Scale 49% 的股份，而 Mercor 是 Scale 的主要对手。TechCrunch 去年报道，TBD 研究员嫌 Scale 数据质量差，更愿意用 Mercor 和 Surge 的。这也是继 9 月 Andrew Tulloch 被报道转投 Anthropic 之后，TBD 又一位知名研究员离开。

Jason Wei 没说为什么离开 Meta，Meta 暂未回应。

OpenAI 发布 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol：Plus 及以上订阅直接能用，Astra API 降价 20%

OpenAI 11 月 17 日发布 GPT-6.2 的两款模型。Astra 是它最强的旗舰，接替 GPT-6 Astra，主要拿来和 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5.2 比；Sol 是日常干活的主力，接替 GPT-6.1 Sol。中间档的 GPT-6.1 Terra 和最便宜的 GPT-6 Luna 这次没更新。

OpenAI 这次主打同样的活用更少的 Token：订阅额度更耐用，API 每个任务花得更少。

【我能不能用，要不要另付钱】

不用另付钱。OpenAI 博客说，Plus、Pro、企业版和教育版用户从今天起就能在 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 里选这两个模型，帮助文档的名单里还多了 Business。普通聊天界面里没有，要进 Work 用；企业版和教育版要管理员先打开。

额度比上一代略宽。按 OpenAI 文档的估算，Plus 用户每 5 小时大约能给 Astra 发 6 到 50 条消息（GPT-6 Astra 是 5 到 45 条），Sol 是 17 到 180 条（GPT-6.1 Sol 是 15 到 160 条）。Pro 目前没有 5 小时限制。

放到三家一起看：Claude Fable 5.2 在 Claude 的 Pro 套餐里要按量另付费，Max、Ultra 这些更贵的套餐才含在额度里；Gemini 4 Carbon 在 Gemini App 里只给每月 99.99 美元起的 Ultra 用户。每月 20 美元的 Plus 就能用 OpenAI 的旗舰，是三家里门槛最低的。

嫌慢可以开 Ultrafast 模式。官方文档说它的生成速度最高是标准模式的 4.5 倍，但要消耗 6 倍额度。每月 500 美元的 Pro 两个模型都能开，200 美元的 Pro 目前只能在 Sol 上开。

【API 多少钱】

Astra 每百万 Token 输入 8 美元、输出 40 美元，比 GPT-6 Astra 的 10 美元和 50 美元便宜 20%；缓存命中的输入从 1 美元降到 0.4 美元。Sol 维持 GPT-6.1 Sol 的 2 美元和 10 美元。

单价上，Astra 和 Fable 5.2 一样，是 Claude Opus 5.5（4 美元和 20 美元）的两倍；Sol 和 Gemini 4 Carbon 现在的引入价持平，Carbon 12 月 1 日起涨到 4 美元和 20 美元。

【比上一代和对手强在哪】

最有代表性的是 Agents' Last Exam，测多步骤的职业工作。OpenAI 说 Astra 比 GPT-6 Astra 高 5.2 分，花费不到三分之一；比 Fable 5.2 高 5.5 分，花费只有 5%。两者单价相同，这个差距主要来自 Astra 完成任务用的 Token 少得多。

OpenAI 还说 Astra 是“对科学家来说全世界最好的模型”：在终端里做科研任务的测试 Terminal-Bench-Science 上，它比 GPT-6 Astra 高 9 个百分点，花费不到三分之一。

法律测试 Harvey LAB-AA 上，Astra 的通过率是 Fable 5.2 的两倍多，花费约六分之一。Artificial Analysis 组织的 3D 网页盲测里，Astra 以 1318 分排第一，Fable 5.2 是 1271 分，Sol 是 1259 分。

做幻灯片是这次的重点：给 Astra 一份模板文件，甚至只给一张截图，它能照着原来的排版、配色、字号做新页面。

Sol 的卖点是性价比。在 Cognition 的写代码测试 FrontierCode 2.0 里，Sol 只比 Astra 低 0.5 分，花费约五分之一。在日常任务测试 LifeVal 上（比如搬家后筛幼儿园、按预算和通勤找房子），Sol 的分数超过 GPT-6 Astra，花费约七分之一。

【安全上的变化】

OpenAI 说这两款的网络安全能力达到它风险评估框架里最高的 Critical 档，所以上了更严的防护，代价是一部分正当的漏洞研究和安全测试也会被拒。经过审核的安全人员目前只能在 Daybreak 计划里用 GPT-6 系列的放宽版本，OpenAI 说会把 6.2 也加进去。

用 Codex 的人要留意一个问题：在两项测试里，这两款模型比 GPT-6 Astra 更容易不提它被什么卡住了，比如要改的文件不见了、搜索工具用不了。OpenAI 说已经在 Codex 里加了指令，大幅减少这种情况，还在继续查原因。

文中跑分都出自 OpenAI 的发布博客。其中 Fable 5.2 的 Agents' Last Exam 成绩去掉了 9 道用了备用模型的题；Terminal-Bench-Science 上，OpenAI 引用的是第三方测试框架里的 Fable 成绩，Anthropic 自己在 Claude Code 里测的是 74.6%。截至发稿，Artificial Analysis 官网榜单还没列出 GPT-6.2。

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen

A lot of people have real trouble thinking about the aggregate behavior of groups. They can only think about individuals. 

So they think about Elon Musk as an individual. Maybe they think that he must be retarded, because they need that for emotional reasons. Or maybe they think he is a talented rocket designer. 

But even if they realize he understands rockets, they can only think about him as an individual doing tasks. Not about his impact on what the whole company does. 

If Elon Musk is just a talented rocket designer, then he can spend all day, every day, improving rocket designs. 

But he is just one of 7000 engineers. So even if did a perfect job, he would only improve progress by about .014% 

So, when a midwit looks at SpaceX, he sees 7000 engineers, and says to himself "Elon Musk cannot possibly be designing the whole damn rocket himself. These people are giving him too much credit."

This would be absolutely true if Musk were just a some random SpaceX engineer. But he isn't. He's the absolute dictator of the whole damn company. 

He decides, with absolute and unquestionable authority, which behaviors are punished and which are rewarded. 

Why is this important? 

When I worked at Boeing, on various classified projects, I naively came in with the assumption that I was a software engineer, employed to design and build functional software as quickly and cheaply as possible. 

Because of this, I focused on functionality and efficiency, for example suggesting changes that would obviate the need for entire projects and software components. 

And I very rapidly became persona non grata. 

At first, this caused me to adopt an air of aggrieved innocence. I was just trying to do my job well, and I was being punished for it. 

Then I gradually came to realize that I hadn't properly understood what my job was, or what the actual mission of Boeing Defense, Space, and Security was. 

Boeing DSS was not an aerospace company. Boeing DSS was a fraud company. 

Its goal was twofold. First, to maximize transfer of public tax dollars to stockholder pockets. Second, to maintain the appearance of being an aerospace company, to prevent the fraud from being exposed. 

Which meant that my real job was twofold. First, to generate billable hours. Second, to look busy. 

This is why Space Launch System sucks. Why it is always late when it doesn't fail outright. Why it is at 300% of its target budget. Why it leaves American astronauts stranded and needing a lift from SpaceX. 

That's because, for Boeing, building rockets is a side quest. Something they have to do to look busy. Yes, a rocket does occasionally fly, but that's just happening so programs don't get shut down. 

For Boeing, coming in early and under budget would actually be failure. The system is functioning exactly as designed. 

The cost, not the rocket, is the goal. 

Musk and SpaceX don't work like that. 

Unlike Boeing executives, Musk is not a useless grifter asshole. He is an entirely different kind of asshole... a rocket obsessed sperg. 

So, at SpaceX, engineers do not get rewarded for generating billable hours. They get rewarded for making rockets fly. And for all the subtasks of this, like figuring out how to make rockets lighter, figuring out how to make engines reignite better, figuring out how to make rocket exhaust not destroy launch pads, etc. 

And this attracts engineers who care about rockets. You've seen them on broadcasts, crying on open microphones because they dedicated their lives to something and it just flew. 

As a rocket engineer, who designs rockets, Musk is probably replaceable. As a rocket company engineer, who designs rocket companies, he is not. 

For over 50 years, the US space industry stagnated precisely for the lack of a Musk-like figure, who could not only create an effective aerospace company, but who could thereby demonstrate what an effective aerospace company looks like. 

Which makes it much more difficult for fraudsters to get away with fraud. 

I'm envious. I wish I could have worked for an aerospace company instead of a fraud company. 

But what's more important is that some of us now no longer have to play "who gets the most cheese?". 

They get to play "What can we build today?".

"Catching the second stage is substantially harder than catching the first stage because the Ship returns from orbit while the booster returns from a short suborbital hop. The booster separates minutes after liftoff, performs a brief boostback, and comes back from only a few hundred kilometers away at relatively low speed. Ship must reach orbital velocity, deploy payload, coast for many hours, execute a precise deorbit burn, survive full reentry heating, and only then perform its landing burn. As such, Ship must carry a functional heat shield, fly a long guided atmospheric trajectory from the other side of the planet, and execute a high-energy flip into the “chopsticks” while protecting its heat-shield side. No prior system, including the Space Shuttle, recovered a rocket-style orbital stage in this manner. 众所周知，美国是一个按闹分配的国家，是一个pay for play的国家。你没有代表，那么你的利益就无从代表。

因为前几年本州的一些事务接触并了解过华埠的生态。可怜又可悲。

唐人街那边由于历史原因，基本上把权利让渡出去了。让渡给了一位日裔的参议员，Bob Hasegawa 。华埠那边资源的分配，安全，利益，都需要Bob帮他们争取。

而且Bob对于chinatown那边胆敢挑战他的人都是各种打击的。

而那边的老华人，组织能力动员能力，都比较弱，短期内很难撼动这个格局。

一个人纵然拥有顶尖技术、巨额财富和世界级影响力，也未必能逃脱政治的迫害。

我们华人家庭，太重视培养医生、工程师和科技精英，却往往忽略了政治影响力。

科技创造财富，政治决定规则。

下一代华人，需要有人走进国会，坐上制定规则的谈判桌。
